definitions.explanation: A set of related events, actions, or things that are connected as a group or sequence. Almost always used as a pre-noun modifier with の.

examples.japanese: {一連|いちれん}の{事件|じけん}を{調|しら}べる。
examples.english: To investigate the series of incidents.

examples.japanese: {一連|いちれん}の{流|なが}れを{説明|せつめい}してください。
examples.english: Please explain the sequence of events.

examples.japanese: {一連|いちれん}の{不祥事|ふしょうじ}により、{社長|しゃちょう}は{辞任|じにん}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: Due to the series of scandals, the company president was forced to resign.

notes:
FORMS:
{一|いち} (one) + {連|れん} (sequence, link) = one connected sequence.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Almost always used as {一連|いちれん}の + noun. It functions as a pre-noun modifier and is rarely used alone as a standalone noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一連|いちれん}の{事件|じけん}: a series of incidents
- {一連|いちれん}の{流|なが}れ: the sequence of events
- {一連|いちれん}の{作業|さぎょう}: a series of tasks
- {一連|いちれん}の{動|うご}き: a series of movements/developments
- {一連|いちれん}の{報道|ほうどう}: a series of news reports
- {一連|いちれん}の{騒動|そうどう}: the whole commotion/incident

USAGE:
{一連|いちれん} emphasizes that the items form a connected whole, not just unrelated individual occurrences. It is common in news and formal writing.
